C0.quote: classic Chamberlin-Courant multiwinner voting rule (CC) on single-peaked preference profiles
C0.note: Winner determination algorithms for multiwinner voting rules.

C1.quote: it runs in almost linear time in the input size
C1.note: All main results are algorithms or ETH/SETH-based lower bounds.

C2.1.value: preference profile / profile / preferences; misrepresentation function; approval ballots; votes
C2.1.quote: is called a preference profile or just a profile or preferences

C2.2.quote: A misrepresentation function r : V × C → R≥0 measures how much
C2.2.note: General misrepresentation or utility functions. Special cases are approval ballots and Borda (linear order); weak orders are allowed.

C2.3.quote: Balloting a misrepresentation function fully is costly for a voter
C2.3.note: Voters are described as having preferences, utilities and misrepresentation values. These are referred to as things voters have and could ballot, but they are not separately notated.

C2.4.quote: A tuple (V, C, r) or (V, C, u) is called a preference profile
C2.4.note: The rule is applied directly to preferences or utilities. There is no statement about reporting.

C4.1.quote: u(v, c) = 1 iff c ∈ Av and u(v, c) = 0
C4.1.note: Approval utility and Borda misrepresentation are defined from the ballots.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: we define total utility of C ′ by u(C ′ )
C5.1.note: The CC and Thiele problems are defined by total voter utility or misrepresentation. This is the rule's own objective.

C5.2.quote: Its dual measure is the utility function u : V × C
C5.2.note: Utility is computed from the input. No statement relates the input to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: a voter v gives an approval ballot as a vote
